name: Ragdoll
funFact: Ragdolls tend to go limp and relaxed when picked up, which is how the breed got its name.
healthNote: Ragdolls are sometimes screened for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, a heart condition worth discussing with a vet.
about: Ragdolls were developed in California in the 1960s and are prized for their striking blue eyes and plush semi-long coat. They're famously docile, often following their owners from room to room and settling happily into a lap for hours.
description: A gentle and affectionate breed that enjoys being close to people.

halloweenRole.title: The Gentle Ghost
halloweenRole.tagline: Drifts from room to room and haunts your lap.

name: Maine Coon
funFact: Maine Coons are one of the largest domesticated cat breeds, with males often reaching 8–9 kg.
healthNote: Maine Coons are commonly screened for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and hip dysplasia given their size.
about: Native to the United States and one of the oldest natural breeds in North America, the Maine Coon is built for cold climates with a shaggy, water-resistant coat and tufted paws. Despite their imposing size, they're known as gentle giants with a playful, dog-like temperament.
description: A large, friendly and playful breed known for its social personality.

halloweenRole.title: The Forest Witch
halloweenRole.tagline: Gentle, confident and quietly powerful.

name: Siamese
funFact: Siamese cats are famously vocal and will happily hold a conversation with you.
healthNote: Siamese cats can be prone to dental issues and certain respiratory sensitivities, so regular checkups are recommended.
about: One of the oldest and most recognizable Asian cat breeds, the Siamese originated in Thailand (formerly Siam) and became popular worldwide for its striking color-point coat and piercing blue eyes. They form intense bonds with their people and aren't shy about voicing their opinions.
description: A vocal and social breed that loves attention and interaction.

halloweenRole.title: The Fortune Teller
halloweenRole.tagline: Always has something to tell you.

name: Bengal
funFact: Bengals descend from crosses with the Asian leopard cat, which gives them their wild-looking coat.
healthNote: Bengals are sometimes monitored for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and progressive retinal atrophy.
about: Bred by crossing domestic cats with the Asian leopard cat, Bengals carry a wild look with a distinctly domestic temperament. They're highly intelligent and athletic, and often enjoy water, climbing and interactive play more than the average housecat.
description: An energetic and curious breed that loves climbing, exploring and playing.

halloweenRole.title: The Night Hunter
halloweenRole.tagline: Wild by moonlight, elegant by nature.

name: British Shorthair
funFact: Their round face and calm grin are often credited as the inspiration for the Cheshire Cat.
healthNote: This breed can be prone to weight gain, so portion control and regular activity are worth keeping an eye on.
about: A classic English breed with roots tracing back to Roman times, the British Shorthair is known for its dense, plush coat and round, teddy-bear face. They're easygoing and independent, content to relax nearby rather than demand constant attention.
description: A calm and independent breed that enjoys company without demanding constant attention.

halloweenRole.title: The Cheshire Cat
halloweenRole.tagline: Unbothered, even by the supernatural.

name: Sphynx
funFact: Despite having no fur, Sphynx cats still need regular baths to manage oil buildup on their skin.
healthNote: Sphynx cats are sometimes screened for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and need extra care to protect their exposed skin from sunburn and cold.
about: Developed in Canada in the 1960s from a natural hairless mutation, the Sphynx is anything but low-maintenance — their bare skin means they crave warmth, sunlight and close physical contact. They're playful and people-oriented, often described as more dog-like than cat-like.
description: An affectionate and outgoing breed that enjoys warmth, attention and company.

halloweenRole.title: The Ancient Spirit
halloweenRole.tagline: No fur, no fear, endless warmth.

name: Persian
funFact: Their long, thick coat needs daily brushing to prevent mats and tangles.
healthNote: Their flat facial structure can be linked to breathing and eye-tearing issues, and they're sometimes screened for polycystic kidney disease.
about: One of the oldest cat breeds, the Persian has been prized for centuries for its luxurious long coat and sweet, gentle expression. They favor a calm, predictable routine and are happiest curled up in a quiet corner of the home.
description: A quiet and affectionate breed that prefers a calm and comfortable environment.

halloweenRole.title: The Vampire Countess
halloweenRole.tagline: High maintenance royalty. Worth it.

name: Abyssinian
funFact: One of the oldest known cat breeds, with a look believed to resemble cats depicted in ancient Egyptian art.
healthNote: Abyssinians are sometimes screened for pyruvate kinase deficiency, a hereditary condition affecting red blood cells.
about: With a lineage often linked to ancient Egypt, the Abyssinian has a distinctive ticked coat that gives it a wild, foxlike appearance. They're endlessly curious and athletic, happiest when given plenty of space to climb, explore and investigate.
description: An intelligent and energetic breed that loves exploring and staying active.

halloweenRole.title: The Ancient Guardian
halloweenRole.tagline: Watchful, wild-eyed and ever curious.

name: American Shorthair
funFact: American Shorthairs are descended from working cats that sailed with early European settlers to keep ships and barns free of rodents.
healthNote: The breed is generally hardy, but is sometimes screened for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and can be prone to weight gain without enough activity.
about: Bred from the sturdy working cats of colonial America, the American Shorthair is an easygoing all-rounder with a dense coat and a broad, friendly face. They adapt to almost any household, staying playful into adulthood without ever being demanding.
description: A relaxed and adaptable breed that fits comfortably into busy family life.

halloweenRole.title: The Barn Watcher
halloweenRole.tagline: Keeps the mice — and the ghosts — in line.

name: Birman
funFact: Every Birman has four white paws, often called "gloves", which are part of the breed standard.
healthNote: Birmans are sometimes screened for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and, in some lines, for a hereditary kidney condition.
about: Wrapped in legend as the sacred temple cat of Burma, the Birman pairs a pale, silky colour-point coat with deep blue eyes and those signature white gloves. They are gentle, people-focused companions who follow you quietly from room to room.
description: A soft-spoken and devoted breed that loves gentle company.

halloweenRole.title: The Temple Keeper
halloweenRole.tagline: Sacred, serene and always watching the door.

name: Burmese
funFact: Nearly every modern Burmese traces back to a single brown cat named Wong Mau, brought to the United States in 1930.
healthNote: Some Burmese lines are screened for hypokalaemia and, in flatter-faced show types, for cranial deformities and dental crowding.
about: Descended from a temple cat of old Burma, the Burmese is heavier than it looks and utterly devoted to its people. They stay kitten-like for years, riding on shoulders, supervising chores and insisting on being part of every conversation.
description: A warm and involved breed that wants to be part of everything you do.

halloweenRole.title: The Shadow That Follows
halloweenRole.tagline: Always one step behind you. On purpose.

name: Cornish Rex
funFact: The Cornish Rex has only the soft, wavy undercoat, which makes its fur feel like crushed velvet.
healthNote: Their thin coat offers little protection, so they need warmth and sun care, and some lines are screened for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
about: Born from a single curly kitten on a Cornish farm in 1950, the Cornish Rex is a lean, arched acrobat with huge ears and a permanent look of mischief. They run hot, love a warm lap and rarely slow down.
description: A high-energy acrobat that turns any room into a racetrack.

halloweenRole.title: The Restless Poltergeist
halloweenRole.tagline: Knocks things off shelves. Blames the wind.

name: Devon Rex
funFact: Devon Rex cats are often nicknamed "pixie cats" or "alien cats" for their huge ears, wide eyes and elfin faces.
healthNote: The breed is sometimes screened for hereditary myopathy and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and its sparse coat needs protection from cold.
about: Discovered in Devon in 1960, this impish breed has loose curls, a slender body and an appetite for climbing to the highest point in any room. Devons bond hard, perch on shoulders and expect to share your dinner.
description: A mischievous shoulder-rider that never wants to be left out.
vibe: Part cat, part bat, all trouble.

halloweenRole.title: The Little Gremlin
halloweenRole.tagline: Big ears, bigger schemes.

name: Exotic Shorthair
funFact: The Exotic Shorthair is often called "the lazy person's Persian" because it has the Persian's face without the daily coat care.
healthNote: Their flat faces can lead to breathing and tear-duct problems, and the breed is commonly screened for polycystic kidney disease.
about: Created by crossing Persians with American Shorthairs, the Exotic keeps the round, sweet-faced Persian look in a dense, plush, easy-care coat. They are quiet, affectionate homebodies who like a predictable day.
description: A gentle, low-key companion with a teddy-bear face.

halloweenRole.title: The Sleepy Gargoyle
halloweenRole.tagline: Guards the house without ever getting up.

name: Norwegian Forest Cat
funFact: Known in Norway as the "skogkatt", this breed appears in Norse legend as the giant cats that pulled the goddess Freya's chariot.
healthNote: The breed is sometimes screened for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, hip dysplasia and glycogen storage disease type IV.
about: Shaped by centuries of Scandinavian winters, the Norwegian Forest Cat has a water-shedding double coat, tufted ears and strong climbing claws. They are calm, confident and affectionate on their own terms, happy to watch the household from a high shelf.
description: A hardy, even-tempered climber built for the cold.

halloweenRole.title: The Forest Guardian
halloweenRole.tagline: Older than the woods, calmer than the storm.

name: Oriental Shorthair
funFact: The Oriental Shorthair comes in over 300 colour and pattern combinations, more than almost any other breed.
healthNote: As a close relative of the Siamese, the breed can be prone to dental disease, and some lines are screened for progressive retinal atrophy and heart conditions.
about: A Siamese in every way but colour, the Oriental Shorthair is a sleek, angular cat with enormous ears and a bottomless need for attention. They talk constantly, open cupboards for sport and fall apart if left alone too long.
description: A loud, clever extrovert that never runs out of things to say.
vibe: Commentary track for your entire life.

halloweenRole.title: The Town Crier
halloweenRole.tagline: Announces every ghost, loudly, at 3am.

name: Russian Blue
funFact: Legend says the Russian Blue's ancestors were ship cats from the port of Arkhangelsk, sailed to Britain in the 1860s.
healthNote: The breed is one of the healthier pedigrees, though it can be prone to weight gain and benefits from measured feeding.
about: Cloaked in a dense, silvery double coat that seems to shimmer, the Russian Blue is reserved with strangers and quietly devoted to its own people. They keep a tidy routine, dislike noise and chaos, and greet you the same way every day.
description: A reserved, elegant cat that bonds deeply with a chosen few.
vibe: Shy at the door. Attached at the couch.

halloweenRole.title: The Silver Phantom
halloweenRole.tagline: Seen for a second, then gone in the mist.

name: Scottish Fold
funFact: Every Scottish Fold traces back to Susie, a white barn cat found in Perthshire in 1961 with unusual folded ears.
healthNote: The gene that folds the ears also affects cartilage throughout the body and can cause a painful degenerative joint disease, so responsible breeding and vet monitoring matter.
about: Famous for ears that fold forward into a rounded, owl-like head, the Scottish Fold is a placid, sweet-natured cat that likes to sit in odd flat poses. They are affectionate without being clingy and settle easily into calm homes.
description: A mellow, owl-faced companion that enjoys quiet company.

halloweenRole.title: The Owl Familiar
halloweenRole.tagline: Perches by the cauldron, blinks slowly, judges softly.

name: Siberian
funFact: Siberians are slow to mature, often taking up to five years to reach their full size and weight.
healthNote: The breed is generally robust but is sometimes screened for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy given its size and build.
about: Russia's national cat, the Siberian spent centuries as a farm and monastery cat, developing a thick triple coat and a fearless, dog-like temperament. They are strong, agile and playful, often fascinated by water and happy to greet visitors.
description: A powerful, friendly breed with a playful, dog-like streak.

halloweenRole.title: The Snow Sentinel
halloweenRole.tagline: Trudges through the storm to check on you.

name: Tonkinese
funFact: The Tonkinese is a deliberate cross of the Siamese and Burmese, blending the look and voice of both.
healthNote: The breed can inherit dental issues and, in some lines, is screened for the heart and eye conditions seen in its parent breeds.
about: A mid-century blend of Siamese and Burmese, the Tonkinese keeps the best of both: aqua eyes, a soft mink coat and a chatty, affectionate personality. They are busy, curious and love a good game of fetch.
description: A sociable, playful breed that splits the difference between its parents.

halloweenRole.title: The Mischief Twin
halloweenRole.tagline: Two breeds' worth of trouble in one coat.

name: Turkish Angora
funFact: White Turkish Angoras often have odd-coloured eyes, one blue and one amber, and the breed is a national treasure protected by Ankara Zoo.
healthNote: White, blue-eyed Angoras can carry hereditary deafness, and the breed is sometimes screened for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and a rare hereditary ataxia.
about: One of the oldest natural semi-longhair breeds, the Turkish Angora has a fine, silky single coat with no heavy undercoat, a plumed tail and a lithe, dancer's build. They are bright, athletic and determined to be in charge of the household.
description: A graceful, energetic breed that runs the house on its own terms.

halloweenRole.title: The Pale Enchantress
halloweenRole.tagline: Moonlit, mismatched eyes that miss nothing.
